summary.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue about INR142 crore and PAT nearly INR60 crore; management guides 15-20% growth for FY27 across the group.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated revenue of about INR142 crore and PAT of nearly INR60 crore, with Coris BioConcept (acquired August 2025) contributing INR35.91 crore for seven months. 3B India molecular diagnostics grew about 10% to INR86.47 crore, below internal projections, which management attributed to a high base from FY25 flu and dengue/chikungunya demand and Middle East disruption to export markets. Standalone non-export revenue grew about 7.1% and exports about 25%, and the company guided to 15-20% growth in FY27 with margins broadly maintained. Coris carries a loss-making first half and is guided to be only slightly EBITDA positive in FY27, while management said M&A is still under way with no deal closed.

segments.name: 3B India molecular diagnostics
segments.commentary: Sales INR86.47 crore in FY26, up about 10% from INR78.34 crore, with non-export domestic growth about 7.1% and exports about INR21.4 crore (includes exports to TRUPCR). Management said domestic growth would be about 15% in a normal year, with the FY25 flu/dengue/chikungunya spike worth about INR4.2 crore.

segments.name: TRUPCR Europe
segments.commentary: FY26 sales GBP1.75 million (INR20.67 crore), up from GBP1.28 million; management cited about 40% CAGR over four years. Its EBITDA margin was described as about 15-20%.

segments.name: Coris BioConcept (Belgium)
segments.commentary: Consolidated from 29 August 2025 with FY26 sales INR35.91 crore and PAT INR8.76 crore, lifted by a one-time HAT order. Management guided to about INR50-52 crore revenue on a full-year basis in FY27 and slightly EBITDA positive, with EBITDA margin of about 10% targeted in FY27-28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% on a consolidated basis; management said EBITDA should grow at a similar 15-20% pace and margin profile should be maintained.

Coris expected to be slightly EBITDA positive in FY27, with the first two quarters loss-making; about 5-7% EBITDA targeted in FY28 and about 10% in FY27-28 per management, with revenue of about INR5 million (about INR50 crore) in FY27.

Management said US FDA clearance for selected AMR products is a process with timing uncertain (1 to 1.5 years or later); the US could contribute about 20% of AMR revenue, about INR11-16 crore (USD1-1.5 million).
Depreciation for FY27 guided at about INR4.5-5 crore for the full year.
Sample-to-answer system (via OEM) expected to start installations at two to three labs from Q3 FY27, with the validation said to be positive; this is included in the 15-20% guidance.
Management intends to keep a reserve of about INR50 crore and deploy the rest into M&A over the next one to two years; a deal was targeted by year-end but no timing was committed.
Company will move to two earnings calls per year (next in the half-year).
capex_capacity: Current capacity utilisation about 50%; management said any capacity increase would cost about INR4-5 crore, so expansion capex is small.
Coris capitalised about INR8 crore of R&D under Belgian law; INR1.6 crore amortised in FY26 at 20% per year, with the R&D capitalisation expected to continue at a somewhat lower scale.
IVDR: BSI appointed as notified body; IVDR-aligned QMS audits completed; technical documentation review progressing for key product families.
demand_pricing: Management said price competition is contained: fierce only in low-priced single tests (TB, HBV, HCV), while multi-panel respiratory and meningitis and oncology are less contested; Chinese players are underpricing respiratory and enteric products.
Management views the Indian molecular diagnostics market at about INR500-600 crore, with the company holding about 15% share; the market is expected to grow 8-10%.
Average selling price to distributors about INR700-800 per kit (range INR300 to INR2,000); distributor markup 15-20%, with hospitals and labs marking up further.
Coris's Resist-5 (AMR product) is about 30-35% of Coris revenue; US rapid AMR diagnostic market estimated around INR100 crore, mainly served by imports.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR21.4 crore export figure include TRUPCR, and what is domestic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the INR21.4 crore includes exports to TRUPCR. Non-export standalone revenue grew about 7.1%; adding back about INR4.2 crore of FY25 flu and chikungunya/dengue sales, domestic growth would be about 12.5-13%.

qa_highlights.question: What is Coris's full-year FY26 revenue on a 12-month basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Coris did about INR50 crore for the full year; with Coris's accounting aligned to 31 March, the 15-month period to March 2026 gave INR57.65 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How does the margin look for FY27 and how is Q1/Q2 Coris loss treated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide quarterly; it said full-year revenue and EBITDA should both grow 15-20%, with Coris losing money in Q1 and Q2 and benefiting from HAT order timing in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the M&A pipeline and cash deployment?
qa_highlights.answer: Two or three opportunities are in advanced discussion with consultants in France, UK and US; European valuations are high, and the company will hold a reserve of INR50 crore with the balance for M&A over one to two years. Treasury is about 90% in FDs, government bonds and AAA corporate bonds, and about 5-7% in equity mutual funds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Coris contract status and the EBITDA trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Of a EUR6 million four-year contract (Congo, affected by Ebola), about EUR3.45 million has been executed and about EUR2.4 million remains; Coris is guided to slightly EBITDA positive in FY27, about 10% in FY27-28.

risks_watch: Coris earnings depend on the HAT order timing; the Congo contract is at risk from the Ebola outbreak.
FY26 domestic growth (~10%) lagged the chains' reported test volume growth of 10-11%; the company said it is high-base affected.
FY27 consolidated margin depends on Coris losses in H1 and the M&A outcome; the cash pile of about INR230 crore is not yet deployed.
Chinese competition in respiratory and enteric products, including export markets, and IVDR compliance timing for EU exports.
US FDA clearance timing for AMR products remains uncertain.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the 15-20% growth guidance and long-term margin profile, but evasive on quarterly phasing, M&A timing and the FDA timeline, repeatedly deferring to full-year figures. Several answers were also unclear on the numbers, with the chairman asking the analyst to check the slide during the Coris Q4 depreciation discussion.
key_quotes: So, growth of 15% to 20% is what is we are trying to achieve and let's look forward to it.
So, we will do only two earning calls every year.
Coris will become slightly EBITDA positive.

adds.what: Sample-to-answer system installations via OEM at two to three labs (demand-side rollout, not company capacity build)

growth.why: Management guides 15-20% consolidated revenue growth and matching EBITDA growth for FY27, backed partly by Coris (guided ~INR50-52 crore revenue), a sample-to-answer OEM rollout from Q3 FY27 and standalone growth of ~7.1%, but no specific new capacity is being added and utilisation is only ~50%.
